findings.issue_text: Third-party HTML goes straight into `posts.cooked` with no whitelist, and `cooked` is rendered unescaped both in the new embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20`, `raw post.cooked`) and everywhere Discourse renders a topic. The `PollFeed` path (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34-35`) passes feed `content` through `CGI.unescapeHTML` and directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with zero filtering — `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` all survive. The `import_remote` path is only partially mitigated: Readability's tag whitelist strips `<script>`, but `attributes: %w[href src]` still permits `href="javascript:..."`.
`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19-21`: `feed_key` is dead code — defined but never used (presumably intended for If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetching). Either wire it up or delete it.

`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3`: `create_table ..., force: true` in a migration will silently drop an existing table. Drop the `force`. Same objection to editing the already-shipped `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to add `force: true` — modifying a released migration is a footgun for anyone mid-upgrade.

`db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`: `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table under an exclusive lock on older PostgreSQL — for large installs this is a multi-minute outage. Consider add-nullable → backfill → set default/not-null.
`app/models/topic_embed.rb:11`: `contents << "..."` mutates the caller's string in place (and will raise on a frozen literal). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `dup`.
`db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6`: `embed_url` as default-length `string` (varchar 255) will raise on longer URLs; `text` with a hashed index is safer.
`lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-30`: if the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires and that URL is throttled forever. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26`: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a spec value; browsers ignore the malformed header (which happens to produce the desired effect). Deleting the header is the correct expression of intent.
`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`: no `<meta charset>` and no `<title>`; imported feed content with non-ASCII will mis-render.

No documentation for the new `embed.js` integration (undocumented `discourseUrl` / `discourseEmbedUrl` globals), and no admin-visible snippet. Also verify `embed.js` and `embed.css.scss` are added to the Sprockets precompile list — they aren't referenced by any existing manifest, so `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` will raise in production if the list wasn't updated (that config file is outside this checkout, so I couldn't confirm).

`db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`: whitespace-only churn plus a removed trailing newline; four files in this PR lose their trailing newline (`embed.css.scss`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`, `topic_retriever.rb`).

`spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:30-33`: assertions inside an `after` hook run for every example in the context and produce confusing failure attribution; prefer explicit assertions or a shared example.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding only cites a file/line range (app/models/post.rb:130-137) but does not state any specific issue or claim to verify against the diff. Without an articulated problem (e.g., a described bug/security flaw/correctness defect), there is nothing concrete to validate as a real, verifiable problem introduced by these lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Third-party HTML goes straight into `posts.cooked` with no whitelist, and `cooked` is rendered unescaped both in the new embed view (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20`, `raw post.cooked`) and everywhere Discourse renders a topic. The `PollFeed` path (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34-35`) passes feed `content` through `CGI.unescapeHTML` and directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with zero filtering — `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` all survive. The `import_remote` path is only partially mitigated: Readability's tag whitelist strips `<script>`, but `attributes: %w[href src]` still permits `href="javascript:..."`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces an explicit bypass of Discourse’s normal “cooking” pipeline/sanitization: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes directly from RSS (`PollFeed` uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization) and is then stored/rendered as-is. The new embed view renders it unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Because `cooked` becomes identical to the unfiltered `raw`, any HTML/JS in the feed content (e.g., `<script>`, event handlers) would survive and be served to clients. Additionally, `import_remote` uses Readability with a tag whitelist but still allows `href` attributes; without scheme validation, `href="javascript:..."` could remain and be rendered.

In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` for each RSS item. `SimpleRSS` items do not guarantee `content` is present (many feeds use `description`, `summary`, etc.), so `i.content` can be `nil`, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError` and crash the scheduled job. There is no nil-guard or fallback field handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19-21`: `feed_key` is dead code — defined but never used (presumably intended for If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetching). Either wire it up or delete it.

adjudication.rationale: In the added `Jobs::PollFeed` class, the `feed_key` method (lines ~19-21) is defined but not referenced anywhere else in the diff: `execute` calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` parses the feed and imports items without using `feed_key`. No other newly-added code calls `poll_feed.feed_key` either (e.g., `TopicRetriever` invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` only). So as shown, `feed_key` is unused/dead code in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3`: `create_table ..., force: true` in a migration will silently drop an existing table. Drop the `force`. Same objection to editing the already-shipped `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to add `force: true` — modifying a released migration is a footgun for anyone mid-upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `force: true` to `create_table` in a new migration (`create_topic_embeds`) and, more importantly, retrofits `force: true` into an existing migration (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`). In Rails, `create_table ..., force: true` will drop an existing table before recreating it, which is a real data-loss risk if the table already exists (e.g., in some environments, reruns/redo, or divergent branches). Editing an already-shipped migration to add this behavior is also a real upgrade footgun because it changes what a fresh migration run would do compared to prior history.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`: `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table under an exclusive lock on older PostgreSQL — for large installs this is a multi-minute outage. Consider add-nullable → backfill → set default/not-null.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-NULL DEFAULT forces a full table rewrite and takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration; additionally enforcing NOT NULL can require a table scan. Since `posts` is typically large, this migration can cause a significant outage on large installs. The suggested staged approach (add nullable/no default → backfill → set default and NOT NULL) mitigates this. This is directly verifiable from the migration content in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/topic_embed.rb:11`: `contents << "..."` mutates the caller's string in place (and will raise on a frozen literal). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `dup`.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents << "..."` does mutate the `contents` argument in place (that is verifiable from the diff), but the diff’s call sites pass freshly constructed strings (`CGI.unescapeHTML(...)` and `doc.content`) that are not reused afterward, and the file does not enable `frozen_string_literal`, so there’s no concrete, demonstrated bug introduced here. The “will raise on a frozen literal” aspect is speculative because nothing in the diff shows a frozen string being passed. This is more of a defensive/style concern than a clear defect in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6`: `embed_url` as default-length `string` (varchar 255) will raise on longer URLs; `text` with a hashed index is safer.

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string` (Rails default `varchar(255)`) and then adds a **unique index** on it. The code stores arbitrary remote URLs directly into this column (`TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` / `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)`), and URLs can exceed 255 characters in practice (e.g., long querystrings/UTM params). On databases that enforce the limit (e.g., PostgreSQL), inserting a >255 URL will raise and break imports/embeds; on others it may truncate and potentially violate uniqueness/correct lookups. This is a real correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-30`: if the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires and that URL is throttled forever. Use `SET key 1 NX EX 60`.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb retrieved_recently? does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process/thread crashes or is killed after setnx succeeds but before expire runs, the key will remain without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail forever for that URL and thus `retrieved_recently?` to return true indefinitely (permanent throttle). Using an atomic SET with NX+EX (or a Lua script) avoids this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26`: `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a spec value; browsers ignore the malformed header (which happens to produce the desired effect). Deleting the header is the correct expression of intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_embeddable` in `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` which sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. `ALLOWALL` is not one of the standardized/recognized X-Frame-Options directives (commonly only `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the deprecated `ALLOW-FROM`), so the header value is malformed and may be ignored or handled inconsistently by browsers. This makes the header ineffective/unreliable as a control, so the finding points to a real correctness/security-related issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`: no `<meta charset>` and no `<title>`; imported feed content with non-ASCII will mis-render.

adjudication.rationale: The new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` omits `<meta charset>` and `<title>`, but this is not a verifiable defect from the diff alone. Rails typically sends an HTTP `Content-Type` header including a charset (commonly UTF-8), and browsers will use that for decoding; lack of a `<meta charset>` does not inherently cause non-ASCII misrendering. Missing `<title>` is also not a correctness/security bug (at most an accessibility/UX nit). The diff does not show any evidence that the response is served without a charset header or that encoding will be wrong.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No documentation for the new `embed.js` integration (undocumented `discourseUrl` / `discourseEmbedUrl` globals), and no admin-visible snippet. Also verify `embed.js` and `embed.css.scss` are added to the Sprockets precompile list — they aren't referenced by any existing manifest, so `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` will raise in production if the list wasn't updated (that config file is outside this checkout, so I couldn't confirm).

adjudication.rationale: The “no documentation / no admin snippet” part is not a verifiable defect from the diff (it’s a product/docs request). However, the asset pipeline concern is grounded in the diff: a new layout (`app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`) calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, and new assets `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` are added, but the diff does not add them to any existing JS/CSS manifest nor to a precompile configuration. Under typical Rails/Sprockets defaults, additional standalone CSS/JS (beyond application.css/js) are not precompiled unless referenced by a manifest or added to `config.assets.precompile`, so `embed.css` (and likely `embed.js` if intended to be served) can trigger an `AssetNotPrecompiled` error in production.

In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, `require_dependency 'email/sender'` is not referenced anywhere in the shown job implementation (the code only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`). However, an unused `require_dependency` is primarily a cleanup/style/performance nit (and may exist for side effects or legacy autoloading expectations), not a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`: whitespace-only churn plus a removed trailing newline; four files in this PR lose their trailing newline (`embed.css.scss`, `loading.html.erb`, `layouts/embed.html.erb`, `topic_retriever.rb`).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show missing trailing newlines (`\ No newline at end of file`) for `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, and it also adds `\ No newline at end of file` to `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` along with whitespace-only churn. However, this is a formatting/style issue rather than a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:30-33`: assertions inside an `after` hook run for every example in the context and produce confusing failure attribution; prefer explicit assertions or a shared example.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the `after` hook inside the `context "success"` does run for every example in that context and could make failures be reported from the `after` block rather than the specific expectation in an `it` block. However, in this diff all examples under that context are intended to be successful responses and to have `X-Frame-Options == "ALLOWALL"`, so the `after` hook is a reasonable way to DRY those shared assertions. This is a test-structure/style preference rather than a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the code.
